packageRules.description: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy publishes v1 as both a 2021 tag (1a947af9992250f3bc2e68ad0754c0b0c11566c9) and a 2024 branch head (4d27395796ac319302594769cfe812bd207490b1). Renovate's github-tags datasource resolves v1 to the tag, so an automated digest update would silently revert the pinned deploy step from the branch head back to 3.5-year-old code — see SECURITY-PIPELINE.md for the full analysis. This action has only ever published v1, so disabling updates here loses no legitimate version bump.
Tailwind CSS v4 is a migration of its own, so its major update stays a deliberate change.
ESLint 10 waits until eslint-plugin-react declares support for it.
Runner image majors move deliberately, in one pull request for all workflows.
Major updates wait in the Dependency Dashboard until someone approves them.

description: ICTU recommendation 7: do not take a new major's first release. Renovate
never proposes X.0.0 for an npm package, so the earliest a major can be
offered is X.0.1 — the first patch, by which point the release has been
used by others. Majors still wait for Dependency Dashboard approval as
well (the rule above): this decides WHICH version may be offered, that
one decides WHETHER it is raised at all, and the assessment R7 asks for is
what the person ticking the box is doing.
allowedVersions applies to every update type of a matched package, not
only majors, which is why the pattern is written to match X.0.0 alone: no
minor or patch release can look like that. Scoped to npm deliberately —
the same pattern against Docker tags (18-alpine) or the github-runner
datasource (ubuntu 26.04) would mean something else entirely.
The cost, stated plainly: a package that publishes X.0.0 and never a patch
is never offered that major. Add a per-package exception with the reason,
the way a deferral is recorded.
minimumReleaseAge repeats the top-level 14 days and changes nothing; it is
here because Semgrep's renovate-missing-minimum-release-age flags a rule
that does not set it locally.
